source.title: Data Valuation Without Training of a Model
source.authors: Nohyun Ki; Hoyong Choi; Hye Won Chung

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own test-accuracy results after removing data selected by a score, a different method for examining how training data affects generalization. It does not test any listed claim version directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports data-pruning outcomes and training-dynamics measurements. Its scored examples are not examples selected for memorization as defined in V8, and it does not test the other mapped versions. Results that only compare the paper's scoring method with other scores are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a data-valuation method, but its results do not test V1–V8. In particular, CG-score measures a change in an NTK-based complexity bound, not the inclusion-dependent probability of correctly predicting an example's own label required by V8. Correlations with difficulty scores do not establish that equivalence. Feldman and Zhang is cited as related work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that CG-score identifies irregular examples, helps select data important for generalization and detect label noise, and relates to learning difficulty. They leave theoretical justification for more general deep networks open.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies data scoring and pruning, rather than the architectures, optimizers, batch sizes, regularizers, model sizes, or trained-network properties in the listed versions. The pruning experiments use ResNets and compare selected removals with random removal and other scoring methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and removal ordering affect the reported pruning outcome. The authors also report that removing many low-scoring examples together can degrade performance because similar typical examples may be removed simultaneously.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing the lowest CG-score examples preserves accuracy within a reported drop below 1% at 40% removal on CIFAR-10 and 20% removal on CIFAR-100. Removing high-scoring examples produces a faster accuracy decline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An NTK-complexity-based data score identifies examples with differing importance for held-out accuracy in these image-classification pruning experiments.

record.problems: The pruning results are largely presented in figures; exact values are stated only for the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 low-score removal results. The main pruning experiment reports five runs and standard deviations, but the paper does not provide exact numeric test accuracies in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows: further pruning comparisons either appear only as figures without text describing the individual outcomes, or compare the CG-score with other valuation methods rather than report a result about the claim's mapped versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under controlled tuning. Using different optimizers for different architectures is not this comparison.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce those effects.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps. Kernel velocity measures a different property.
Removing examples ranked by inclusion-dependent memorization and comparing accuracy losses with equal-sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: The six rows can remain as related findings, but are not evidence for the listed versions. Appendix D.3 specifies class-balanced pruning and equal training iteration counts across pruning conditions. Additional architecture and fine-tuning experiments also evaluate CG-score, without establishing the memorization criterion required by V8.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning and decay recipes.
Large-batch versus small-batch performance under epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the train-test gap.
Removal of examples selected for memorization and comparison with random removals.
